chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Rahman from Abd Allah ibn Sinan said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Muhrim (one in Ihram) may apply kohl if he has an eye ailment, provided the kohl does not contain saffron.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: One in the state of Ihram (consecration)
key_terms.رَمِدَ: To have an eye ailment or soreness
key_terms.يَكْتَحِلُ: To apply kohl to the eyes

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram use eye drops or kohl during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of fragrance in Ihram extends to topical applications like kohl, specifically excluding saffron due to its distinct scent. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between medicinal utility and aromatic properties, ensuring that the state of Ihram remains valid while allowing for necessary medical care.
